extracted.intended_audience: news organization executives, editors, and legal counsel (Associated Press members and litigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and operational/legal requirements governing a cooperative news-wire service: membership rules, distribution methods, confidentiality/exclusivity, prioritization of dispatches, and what constitutes wrongful appropriation or piracy (as alleged in litigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-operative institution and cost-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The Associated Press is a purely co-operative institution, existing for the benefit and protection of its members. It does not sell its news or make any profit from the same, but divides the cost of gathering and distributing the same equitably among its members.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the organizational model and financial rationale: members jointly bear the expense of gathering news; the value proposition is membership access rather than sale of news. (Used to justify exclusivity and protections.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership representation and publication limits
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The members of The Associated Press are representatives of leading morning and evening newspapers... a member shall publish the news of The Associated Press only in the newspaper, language and place specified in his certificate of membership.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is tied to a specified newspaper, language, and place; by-laws restrict members to publishing AP news only as specified in their membership certificate. Example: morning vs evening papers distinction; practical effect is territorial/format-limited rights to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive use of the budget of news by members
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is of vital importance to the integrity, usefulness and efficiency of The Associated Press and even to its existence as a co-operative organization that its members shall have the sole use for publication of the budget of news which they... have been at the cost and expense of gathering.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy/requirement that the gathered "budget" of news be used solely by contributing members; prevents non-members from appropriating and publishing that same assembled service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and prohibition on advance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No member shall furnish or permit anyone... to furnish to any person who is not a member, news of the corporation in advance of publication, or conduct his business in such a manner that the news furnished by the corporation may be communicated to any person... not entitled to receive the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By-law requirement that members and their employees not disclose AP material to non-members prior to authorized publication. Example/anti-pattern: permitting employees to supply news to outsiders or to copy telegraph output for non-members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness of service as essential value
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The value of the service rendered by The Associated Press to its members largely depends upon the promptness of the service...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational desideratum: rapid transmission and delivery (day service vs night service) are core to the news-wire's value. Examples: day service delivered for immediate publication in afternoon papers; night service for various editions of morning papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and impartiality of news furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The value of the service... largely depends upon the promptness of the service and the accuracy and impartiality of the news furnished'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard that news must be accurate and impartial. The affidavit even mentions an instance of error (confusion of names) illustrating both the expectation and the need for correction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority classification of dispatches (flash, bulletin, despatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit explains news-service parlance and priority: 'A flash is one of the most important telegrams and indicates that the news is of the highest importance... The word "Bulletin" preceding such a despatch indicates... particularly important and pressing character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational rule: messages are categorized by urgency/importance; 'flash' has precedence over everything, 'bulletin' indicates particularly important items. These classifications determine transmission priority and treatment by receiving editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive early transmission to members (time advantage)
rubrics_metrics.description: '...the requirement that the news of the day shall be thus transmitted by The Associated Press to its members earlier than similar information can be furnished to other competing newspapers...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership confers a time-based competitive advantage: members must receive the service earlier than non-members. Preventing rivals from obtaining or publishing the same information first is crucial to member value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against misappropriation/copying from AP sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit details that defendant 'has taken from such edition such news as was available and send it out to its clients as its own news, either textually following the despatches of The Associated Press or rephrasing them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard that copying from AP bulletins, early editions, bulletin boards, or printed telegraph output and reusing that content for resale or to clients constitutes wrongful appropriation. Numerous concrete examples are provided (London bulletins, Captain Duffy statement, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against obtaining news by corrupt or surreptitious means (bribery/corruption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation that defendant obtained 'the news... in large part by bribing and corrupting employees of members... inducing them by such bribery and corruption to secretly and furtively furnish to the defendant the current news of the day as supplied by The Associated Press to its members.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical/legal standard: acquiring news via bribery, secret payments, coded tips, or corrupt arrangements with employees violates membership obligations and constitutes actionable misconduct; example: Cleveland arrangement with telegraph editors paid about ten dollars per week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against false attribution / representing appropriated news as own
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The news thus obtained from The Associated Press by the defendant has been sold to its clients as its own, and as if obtained from original independent sources, and has been credited in the newspapers of such clients to the International News Service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement to attribute sources truthfully; selling or crediting appropriated AP material as if gathered independently or crediting it to the wrong service is wrongful and misleading to the public and clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational distribution methods and local offices' role
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In the City of New York such service of news to its members is furnished by The Associated Press by bulletins sent by messenger, by telephone, and over telegraph lines... similar methods are used... in many of the important cities The Associated Press having its own office which attends to the distribution of the news of the members located in such cities respectively.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes legitimate operational channels for distributing the wire: messenger, telephone, telegraph, and local offices that manage distribution to members—this underpins expectations about how and when members get news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreparable harm from continued piracy and need for injunctive relief
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Similar misappropriations will... be made until defendant is enjoined, and it is of the greatest importance to the complainant, in order to save it and its members from irreparable loss, that defendant be enjoined forthwith.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal standard/practical criterion: ongoing unauthorized appropriation of a news-wire's content inflicts irreparable injury to the cooperative membership model and justifies immediate injunctive relief to prevent future harm.
